dct_description_sm: With increasing temperatures in the high Arctic, understanding the implications for both the physical and biological environment is imperative.  In the high Arctic, studies of the effects of climate change on permafrost have been well documented. However, the concurrent effects of this change on the local vegetation have not been examined as thoroughly.  Not only will this change have repercussions for the persistence of particular species, but it will also affect how they function within their environment.  We are particularly interested in examining changes in the flowering and leaf phenology of vascular plants due to shifts in soil temperature in thermokarst (melt) regions.  We expect large differences in phenological timing (particularly for flowering) between the undisturbed polar desert and thermokarst areas.  By including measures on the evolutionary history of plant communities, we can assess whether soil temperature change is driving this shift in phenology while taking into consideration the shifts in community composition between melt and non-melt areas.
dct_title_s: Phenology data of vascular plants on a thermokarst area of Ellesmere Island, Nunavut
